briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis: Call to Elevate to 'Global Health Emergency'
sections.content: Over the past eight years, 3 million people worldwide have died due to heatwaves, and a Lancet report, which linked 68% of heatwave deaths since the Paris Agreement to climate change, warned of the severity of the situation [1, 12, 204]. The report defines climate change as a 'global health emergency,' and 146 experts are urging its official declaration in response to record-breaking high temperatures [176, 177, 180, 184, 186, 191, 192, 197, 198, 200, 203]. Furthermore, atmospheric greenhouse gas concentrations have reached unprecedented highs [18], and climate change is threatening our society in various ways, not only accelerating health damage but also increasing gun violence in the U.S. [8], causing a 36% surge in pine wilt disease in Gyeonggi Province [11], and raising the risk of large-scale wildfires [14], among others [3, 207]. The United Nations (UN) also warned that the ocean's carbon absorption capacity is weakening due to intensifying climate change, emphasizing that the cost of delaying global climate action is loss of life and deteriorating health [179, 185].

sections.title: ⚠️ Economic Challenges and Tasks of Carbon Neutrality Transition
sections.content: The Bank of Korea projected that achieving carbon neutrality will require a massive investment of 840 trillion KRW, which is expected to lead to an average annual growth rate decline of 0.06-0.07 percentage points and a producer price increase of 0.04 percentage points by 2060 [4, 17, 33, 38, 39, 40, 41, 44, 52, 53, 55, 59, 63, 64, 65, 67, 76, 91, 99, 103, 106, 113]. Profitability in traditional manufacturing sectors such as steel and cement is particularly expected to decline significantly, emphasizing the necessity of a 'just transition' in this process [23, 26]. Globally, the economic damage from climate change is already materializing, with an annual GDP loss of 1 trillion USD and 1 trillion USD in losses due to heatwaves [2, 3], among other impacts [178, 182, 211, 212]. While some question whether delaying carbon neutrality might offer economic benefits, the argument that long-term damages from climate change must also be considered is gaining traction [42].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Technological Innovation
sections.content: Domestically, Jeju Island is soliciting proposals for 'Carbon Neutral Leading Villages' worth 11.2 billion KRW, encouraging resident participation, and building local carbon reduction models [27, 28, 29, 47, 54, 68, 73, 79, 82, 88, 96, 98, 102, 105, 111]. Gwacheon City hosted a 'Carbon Neutral Sharing Day,' leading efforts to share and disseminate citizens' everyday carbon neutrality practices, such as apartment energy saving and corporate resource circulation, and ranked first in Gyeonggi Province for carbon neutrality point system participation [30, 31, 43, 48, 71, 72, 104, 108, 112]. Companies are also strengthening their carbon neutrality goals; BYD joined the UN Global Compact, announcing its commitment to achieving carbon neutrality across its entire value chain by 2045 [58, 60, 66, 81, 90, 100, 101, 107], while KOGAS is contributing to carbon neutrality through various methods such as creating ecological forests [45, 70, 75, 114], and Samchully is sharing CCUS and e-methane trends and supporting industries [49, 85, 86, 87, 89]. Carbon neutrality solutions through technological innovation, such as AI-based smart farms [37], recycling of discarded banners [74, 84], semiconductor greenhouse gas reduction technology [83], and exploring healthy housing technologies [24], are also being actively discussed, and expectations are growing that Artificial Intelligence (AI) could be part of the climate change solution, according to COP31 pledges [50, 56, 61, 93, 189].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Renewable Energy Expansion: Opportunities and Grid Challenges
sections.content: Korea is preparing for a major overhaul of its electricity market as it approaches the era of 100 GW renewable energy capacity [116, 132], and the Ministry of Climate is showing a strong commitment to expansion, demanding large-scale investments in renewable energy and mega-projects for the 2027 budget [115]. Shinhan Bank is investing 250 billion KRW in renewable energy and productive finance funds, supporting both residents and businesses [118, 122, 148, 150, 151, 163, 166, 170], while platforms like 'Mohat' are attracting individual investments in solar power generation projects, surpassing 100 billion KRW in cumulative power generation revenue and expanding the renewable energy sharing market [145, 149, 165, 173]. Furthermore, local governments such as Jeonnam Gwangju and Haenam County are intensifying efforts to become hubs for advanced industries based on renewable energy by easing solar panel setback regulations, establishing RE100 industrial ecosystems, and attracting the integrated headquarters of the five major power generation companies [120, 130, 134, 139, 143, 144, 146, 153, 155, 156, 158, 159, 161, 164, 168, 169]. However, despite the emphasis on renewable energy expansion, grid investment remains stagnant, leading to 'hidden bottlenecks' where rural solar power generation faces difficulties due to transmission network issues or solar electricity is curtailed [131, 135, 140, 167]. This serves as a national security test, as grid instability could lead to manufacturing shutdowns [132], making the strengthening of grid infrastructure an urgent task alongside renewable energy expansion.

sections.title: 🔴 International Community's Climate Action and Responsibility
sections.content: The United Nations (UN) warned that the ocean's carbon absorption capacity is weakening as climate change intensifies [179], and pointed out that despite the awareness for 20 years that the climate crisis would devastate economies, action has been delayed [178, 212]. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) was mentioned as part of the climate change solution in COP31 pledges [189], concerns are rising in the U.S. due to the possibility of climate policy setbacks, such as former President Trump's declaration to abolish Biden-era methane emission regulations [210]. Furthermore, criticisms that the UK relied on 2 billion pounds of 'dubious accounting' to meet its climate aid targets [213, 214], and that domestic public enterprises accumulated achievements with 'faulty carbon credits' suspected of exaggerating reduction effects [175], raise fundamental questions about the transparency and accountability of climate action. Thus, while the international community recognizes the severity of climate change and is engaged in various discussions [15, 13, 22, 190, 194, 196, 199, 201, 202, 205, 208, 209], continuous attention and effort are required to translate these into tangible and responsible actions.

briefing.closing: The severity of the climate crisis and the challenges of transitioning to carbon neutrality, which we discussed in today's briefing, clearly illustrate the reality we face. Now is a critical moment for global solidarity and responsible action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
